## Upstream changes 19.5.5 -> 19.5.6

**Verdict:** NEEDS ATTENTION — no release notes could be found for this version range, so the upgrade cannot be verified; the registry image metadata is also unreadable, so there is nothing to cross-check against either.

### Breaking changes
- none found in the notes — the notes themselves could not be retrieved at all (see Notes read below). This is not the same as upstream confirming no breaking changes; it means the claim cannot be checked from this material.

### Variables
- none found in the notes. The compose file and .env.example are unchanged in structure between these two versions as far as supplied material shows; no renamed, removed, or newly-required variables are evidenced.

### Data and dependencies
- none found in the notes for this range.
- Already true at the current version (19.5.5 baseline, not a change introduced by this upgrade): the compose file pins `postgres:17` and a raised `max_locks_per_transaction=256` with `shared_buffers=256MB`, per the comment "GitLab's schema load and migrations exhaust PostgreSQL's default lock table ... GitLab's external-database guidance calls for a raised max_locks_per_transaction." This is an existing requirement the template already runs under, not something this range raises — no notes were available to say otherwise.

### Before applying
- Since no release notes were readable, treat this as an unverified patch upgrade and check by hand before applying:
  - Read the GitLab 19.5.6 entry directly from the GitLab EE CHANGELOG or the "GitLab 19.5.6 released" post on the GitLab blog/docs site, since the notes source (gitlabhq/gitlabhq releases) returned nothing for this range.
  - Check GitLab's own `UPGRADING.md` / upgrade-path documentation for anything flagged between 19.5.5 and 19.5.6 specifically (background migrations, post-deployment migrations, required intermediate stops).
  - Take a database and config backup before upgrading, as standard practice for any GitLab version bump, since no notes are available to say this one is exempt.
  - Confirm the digest you intend to pin (`GITLAB_IMAGE_VERSION=19.5.6-ee.0@sha256:...`) resolves and matches what GitLab actually published for that tag — the registry lookup failed here, so this has not been confirmed.

### Notes read
- None. The release-notes source reported "no releases between 19.5.5 and 19.5.6 found under gitlabhq/gitlabhq (0 releases read), and no tag range compared." No UPGRADING/BREAKING_CHANGES/CHANGELOG section was supplied for this range either. The registry image comparison also failed (HTTP 404), so the "what the images differ in" section could not inform this review. Everything above the baseline note is drawn solely from the supplied compose file and .env.example, not from release notes.

## Upstream changes 2026.11.1 -> 2026.11.2

**Verdict:** SAFE TO APPLY — patch release, all entries are integration bugfixes and dependency bumps; the image configuration itself is unchanged.

### Breaking changes
- none found in the notes

### Variables
- none — no new, renamed or removed variables. `.env.example` still shows `HOMEASSISTANT_IMAGE_VERSION=2026.11.1` as an example only; the compose file's `x-images` default is what actually governs the pin and must be bumped to `2026.11.2` (with its digest) for the upgrade to take effect.

### Data and dependencies
- none. The notes list only per-integration library bumps (midea-local, reolink_aio, velbus-aio, aiowebostv, frontend, Todoist SDK, aioftp, etc.) and bugfixes. No companion service (database, cache, search engine) version is named anywhere in this range, so the SAFE-TO-APPLY-withholding rule does not trigger.
- If any of the affected integrations are in use — UniFi, ONVIF, Hue, webOS TV, MQTT, Axis, Alexa Devices, Reolink, FRITZ!OS, Spotify, SmartThings, Jellyfin, Proxmox — their fixes apply automatically; no action is required beyond the normal restart.

### Before applying
- Take the usual Home Assistant backup/snapshot before any version bump (standard practice, not specifically called for by these notes).
- Update the pinned digest/tag in the compose file's `x-images` block (`homeassistant/home-assistant:2026.11.2@sha256:...`) since that block, not `.env`, is the source of truth for the running version.
- No manual migration commands, no config edits are indicated by the notes.

### Notes read
- `2026.11.2` (2026-11-16) — full release notes as supplied above.
- `2026.11.1` (2026-11-09) — read only as the baseline for the FROM version, per instructions.
